cards.text: Catch-up time, friend. Haman, the king's top official, just had a gallows built so Mordecai, Queen Esther's cousin, can be hanged on it (Esther 3:1; 2:7; 5:14). But that night, the king can't sleep.

cards.question: King Xerxes can't sleep. What does he order brought in and read to him?

cards.text: When I couldn't sleep in the junk drawer, I counted the dust falling. The king gets somebody reading him old records, and one of them is about a plot: Bigthana and Teresh, two eunuchs who guarded his entrance, had conspired to assassinate him.

cards.question: The records say Mordecai was in on the plot to assassinate King Xerxes.
King Xerxes asks what honor Mordecai got for exposing the plot. His attendants say ___ has been done for him.

cards.text: The man stops a plot to kill the king and gets NOTHING, not even a thank-you card. Years of good batches, and my thank-you was the back of a junk drawer, so Mordecai, I SEE you.

cards.question: Then King Xerxes asks who is in the court. Who's standing there?
Haman just came into the outer court to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows.

cards.text: "Bring him in," orders the king, and in walks Haman with gallows on his mind. Friend, he has NO idea what's on the king's.
The king asks him, "What should be done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor?"

cards.question: King Xerxes asks Haman what should be done for the man the king is delighted to honor. Who does Haman think the king means?

cards.text: Haman's actual thought: "Whom would the king be delighted to honor more than me?" This man hears somebody's getting a prize and starts clearing a spot on his shelf.

cards.question: Haman starts his wish list. He asks for a royal robe the king himself has ___ and a horse with a royal crest that the king himself has ___.
In Haman's plan, who dresses the honored man and parades him on the horse through the city square?

answers.text: One of the king's most noble princes
The captain of the royal guard
One of the queen's own attendants

cards.question: In Haman's plan, the honored man rides through the city square in silence, with no one announcing anything.

cards.text: A robe, a horse, a prince and a parade with an announcer. Haman didn't answer the question, he planned a whole FESTIVAL, and he's sure it's for himself.
The king hears Haman's whole plan. Then he tells Haman to hurry and do just as he proposed.

cards.question: King Xerxes tells Haman to take the robe and the horse to the man he wants to honor. Who is it?

cards.text: MORDECAI?! Haman walked in to get Mordecai hanged, and now he's walking out to throw Mordecai a parade.

cards.question: King Xerxes tells Haman it's fine to skip any part of the plan he'd rather not do.
So Mordecai is dressed in the robe and paraded through the city square. Who shouts "This is what is done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor!" in front of him?

cards.text: Haman wrote that line for himself, and now he's yelling it for Mordecai all over the city square. That's writing your own retirement speech and then getting handed the mic at your rival's party.

cards.question: After the parade, Mordecai goes back to the king's gate.
But Haman rushes home with his head covered in ___.

cards.text: Mordecai gets a parade and goes right back to his spot like it's no big deal. Haman ducks home like somebody who just sent a message to the WRONG group chat.
Haman tells his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that happened. That's the same crowd who told him to build the gallows in the first place (Esther 5:14).

cards.question: This time, Haman's wife Zeresh and his advisers have very different advice. What do they tell him?

answers.text: He will surely fall before Mordecai
He should build a taller gallows
He should ask the king for help

cards.question: Zeresh and the advisers say Haman won't prevail against Mordecai, since Mordecai is ___.
While they're still talking with Haman, the king's eunuchs arrive. Where do they rush him off to?

cards.text: Poor Haman can't even finish a conversation before he's rushed out the door. And that's where we'll leave him for now, friend, because this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the answer card 5 just gave (nothing was done for Mordecai, 6:3). It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card carrying a joke rather than a joke riding on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This card lists what cards 13 to 15 already covered (robe, horse, prince, parade with an announcer) and adds nothing new from 6:7-9. It is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card says the king tells Haman to "do just as he proposed." That gives away card 4, which asks whether the king says it's fine to skip any part of the plan.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card reacts to card 2's answer and adds nothing new from 6:10, so it is a recap card. Its line "now he's walking out to throw Mordecai a parade" also gives away card 5, which asks who shouts the proclamation in front of Mordecai (Haman himself).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card only reacts to card 5's answer (Haman shouts the line for Mordecai, 6:11) and does not move the passage forward. It is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This card retells 6:12, which cards 7 and 8 already asked, so it is a recap card. It also says Mordecai goes back to his spot "like it's no big deal," which states his attitude as fact. The text only says he returned to the king's gate.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The question calls what Zeresh and the advisers say "advice," but in 6:13 they are not advising Haman. They tell him he will not prevail and will surely fall. Because of this framing, the right answer is a prediction while both wrong answers are advice ("He should build a taller gallows" and "He should ask the king for help"), so the right answer stands out as a different kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Nothing in the walkthrough mentions that Esther invited the king and Haman to a banquet (Esther 5:8, 5:12). The baker has no context to reason toward "The banquet Esther prepared" over "The king's throne room," so the answer depends on luck. The opening card's catch-up mentions only the gallows.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
